title: How sponge cities could prevent floods“
titleChinese: 海绵城市”如何“吸水”防涝？
paragraphs: Devastating floods are becoming more and more common around the world. The warming climate is leading to heavier rainfall, but could the way that cities are growing be making things worse? Could we design cities in a different way to reduce the risk of flooding?

As cities expand, and more and more land is underneath concrete or paving, less water is absorbed and more needs to be channelled away by storm drains and sewerage systems. As they become overwhelmed by the volume of water, the risk of flash flooding increases.

Could it be that we've been taking the wrong approach? Chinese landscape architect Yu Kongjian certainly thinks so. In 2013, he proposed the concept of 'sponge cities', which are designed to soak up water – like a sponge – reducing the risk of sudden floods. Natural solutions are encouraged, using riverside parks and ponds to absorb floodwater. Approaches inspired by this have been taken by cities across the world. Auckland, in New Zealand, was named the spongiest city in one study. It has replaced the concrete culverts around the Oakley creek stream with green banks and connected parks. This has reduced flooding in the nearby residential areas as well as the amount of associated contamination which used to be washed into the sea.

Auckland has taken a natural approach, but a much more high-tech method can be seen in Amsterdam. The Dutch city has installed blue-green roofs on a number of buildings. These roofs have a layer of plants on the outside, and then layers underneath which collect and store rainwater. This water can be used by people in the building below to water plants or flush toilets. Sophisticated software can even tell the roofs to release water ahead of upcoming storms to maximise the system's ability to soak up rainwater. It can even identify which areas of the city are at most risk and tailor the response accordingly.

Yu Kongjian describes the sponge city approach as using Tai Chi with nature instead of boxing. Questions have been raised as to whether a natural approach is sufficient when faced with increased rain fall globally. What remains to be seen is whether increased scale and combination with modern technology can help natural methods save many more people from flooding.

vocabulary.entry: **devastating** /ˈdevəsteɪtɪŋ/ adj. 毁灭性的，破坏性极大的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The earthquake had a devastating effect on the region.
vocabulary.translation: 地震对该地区造成了毁灭性的影响。

vocabulary.entry: **flood** /flʌd/ n. 洪水
vocabulary.example: The floods destroyed thousands of homes.
vocabulary.translation: 洪水摧毁了数千所房屋。

vocabulary.entry: **rainfall** /ˈreɪnfɔːl/ n. 降雨量，降雨
vocabulary.example: The region receives very little rainfall.
vocabulary.translation: 该地区降雨量极少。

vocabulary.entry: **concrete** /ˈkɒŋkriːt/ n. 混凝土
vocabulary.example: The building is made of steel and concrete.
vocabulary.translation: 这座建筑是用钢筋混凝土建造的。

vocabulary.entry: **paving** /ˈpeɪvɪŋ/ n. 铺砌路面，铺筑材料
vocabulary.example: The paving in the courtyard needs to be replaced.
vocabulary.translation: 庭院里的铺砌路面需要更换了。

vocabulary.entry: **channel** /ˈtʃænl/ v. 引导，疏导
vocabulary.example: Water is channelled through a series of pipes.
vocabulary.translation: 水通过一系列管道被引导输送。

vocabulary.entry: **storm drain** /ˈstɔːm dreɪn/ n. 雨水排水管，雨水沟（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The storm drains were blocked by leaves.
vocabulary.translation: 雨水排水管被树叶堵塞了。

vocabulary.entry: **sewerage** /ˈsuːərɪdʒ/ n. 污水系统，下水道系统（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The city needs to upgrade its sewerage infrastructure.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市需要升级其污水系统基础设施。

vocabulary.entry: **overwhelmed** /ˌəʊvəˈwelmd/ adj. 被淹没的，不堪重负的
vocabulary.example: The emergency services were overwhelmed by the number of calls.
vocabulary.translation: 紧急服务部门被大量的电话淹没了。

vocabulary.entry: **flash flooding** /ˌflæʃ ˈflʌdɪŋ/ n. 暴洪，突发性洪水（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Flash flooding can occur very quickly after heavy rain.
vocabulary.translation: 暴雨过后暴洪可能很快就会发生。

vocabulary.entry: **landscape architect** /ˈlændskeɪp ˌɑːkɪtekt/ n. 景观设计师（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The landscape architect designed the park to blend with the surrounding area.
vocabulary.translation: 景观设计师设计的公园与周边环境融为一体。

vocabulary.entry: **sponge city** /ˈspʌndʒ ˈsɪti/ n. 海绵城市（专业术语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The sponge city concept uses natural methods to manage rainwater.
vocabulary.translation: 海绵城市理念使用自然方法管理雨水。

vocabulary.entry: **soak up** /ˈsəʊk ʌp/ phr. v. 吸收（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The soil can soak up a lot of water after heavy rain.
vocabulary.translation: 暴雨过后土壤能吸收大量水分。

vocabulary.entry: **riverside** /ˈrɪvəsaɪd/ adj. 河边的，河畔的
vocabulary.example: We went for a walk along the riverside path.
vocabulary.translation: 我们沿着河边小路散步。

vocabulary.entry: **culvert** /ˈkʌlvət/ n. 涵洞，暗渠（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The stream flows through a culvert under the road.
vocabulary.translation: 溪流通过道路下方的涵洞流过。

vocabulary.entry: **residential** /ˌrezɪˈdenʃl/ adj. 住宅的，居民区的
vocabulary.example: They live in a quiet residential area.
vocabulary.translation: 他们住在一个安静的住宅区。

vocabulary.entry: **contamination** /kənˌtæmɪˈneɪʃn/ n. 污染，污染物（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The contamination of the water supply was a serious problem.
vocabulary.translation: 供水污染是一个严重的问题。

vocabulary.entry: **blue-green roof** /ˌbluː ˈɡriːn ruːf/ n. 蓝绿屋顶（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Blue-green roofs help manage rainwater and provide green space.
vocabulary.translation: 蓝绿屋顶有助于管理雨水并提供绿色空间。

vocabulary.entry: **underneath** /ˌʌndəˈniːθ/ adv. 在下面，在底下
vocabulary.example: The pipes run underneath the floor.
vocabulary.translation: 管道铺设在地板下面。

vocabulary.entry: **flush** /flʌʃ/ v. 冲（马桶）
vocabulary.example: Remember to flush the toilet after you use it.
vocabulary.translation: 用完厕所后记得冲水。

vocabulary.entry: **sophisticated** /səˈfɪstɪkeɪtɪd/ adj. 精密的，复杂的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The system uses sophisticated software to predict weather patterns.
vocabulary.translation: 该系统使用复杂的软件来预测天气模式。

vocabulary.entry: **maximise** /ˈmæksɪmaɪz/ v. 最大化，充分利用（书面语）
vocabulary.example: We need to maximise the use of available resources.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要最大限度地利用可用资源。

vocabulary.entry: **tailor** /ˈteɪlə(r)/ v. 调整，使适应（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The training is tailored to individual needs.
vocabulary.translation: 培训是根据个人需求量身定制的。

vocabulary.entry: **Tai Chi** /ˌtaɪ ˈtʃiː/ n. 太极
vocabulary.example: Tai Chi is a gentle form of exercise.
vocabulary.translation: 太极是一种温和的运动形式。

vocabulary.entry: **sufficient** /səˈfɪʃnt/ adj. 足够的，充分的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Is the funding sufficient to complete the project?
vocabulary.translation: 资金是否足够完成这个项目？

vocabulary.entry: **scale** /skeɪl/ n. 规模，范围
vocabulary.example: The scale of the problem is enormous.
vocabulary.translation: 问题的规模是巨大的。

sentences.english: Devastating floods are becoming more and more common around the world.
sentences.chinese: 毁灭性的洪水在世界各地变得越来越普遍。

sentences.english: The warming climate is leading to heavier rainfall, but could the way that cities are growing be making things worse?
sentences.chinese: 气候变暖导致降雨量增加，但城市的发展方式是否会让情况变得更糟？

sentences.english: Could we design cities in a different way to reduce the risk of flooding?
sentences.chinese: 我们能否以不同的方式设计城市来降低洪水风险？

sentences.english: As cities expand, and more and more land is underneath concrete or paving, less water is absorbed and more needs to be channelled away by storm drains and sewerage systems.
sentences.chinese: 随着城市的扩张，越来越多的土地被混凝土或铺砌路面覆盖，吸收的水分减少，更多的水需要通过暴雨排水沟和下水道系统疏导。

sentences.english: As they become overwhelmed by the volume of water, the risk of flash flooding increases.
sentences.chinese: 当它们被大量的水淹没时，暴洪的风险就会增加。

sentences.english: Could it be that we've been taking the wrong approach?
sentences.chinese: 会不会是我们采用了错误的方法？

sentences.english: Chinese landscape architect Yu Kongjian certainly thinks so.
sentences.chinese: 中国景观设计师俞孔坚确实这么认为。

sentences.english: In 2013, he proposed the concept of 'sponge cities', which are designed to soak up water – like a sponge – reducing the risk of sudden floods.
sentences.chinese: 2013年，他提出了"海绵城市"的概念，旨在像海绵一样吸收水分，降低突发洪水的风险。

sentences.english: Natural solutions are encouraged, using riverside parks and ponds to absorb floodwater.
sentences.chinese: 鼓励采用自然解决方案，利用河滨公园和池塘吸收洪水。

sentences.english: Approaches inspired by this have been taken by cities across the world.
sentences.chinese: 世界各地的城市都采用了受此启发的方案。

sentences.english: Auckland, in New Zealand, was named the spongiest city in one study.
sentences.chinese: 新西兰的奥克兰在一项研究中被评为最"海绵"的城市。

sentences.english: It has replaced the concrete culverts around the Oakley creek stream with green banks and connected parks.
sentences.chinese: 它用绿色河岸和相连的公园取代了奥克利溪流周围的混凝土涵洞。

sentences.english: This has reduced flooding in the nearby residential areas as well as the amount of associated contamination which used to be washed into the sea.
sentences.chinese: 这减少了附近居民区的洪水，也减少了过去会被冲入大海相关污染物的数量。

sentences.english: Auckland has taken a natural approach, but a much more high-tech method can be seen in Amsterdam.
sentences.chinese: 奥克兰采用了自然的方法，但在阿姆斯特丹可以看到一种更高科技的方法。

sentences.english: The Dutch city has installed blue-green roofs on a number of buildings.
sentences.chinese: 这座荷兰城市在许多建筑上安装了蓝绿屋顶。

sentences.english: These roofs have a layer of plants on the outside, and then layers underneath which collect and store rainwater.
sentences.chinese: 这些屋顶外部有一层植物，植物下面的一些层（比如过滤层、储水层、根阻层和防水膜）被用来收集和储存雨水。

sentences.english: This water can be used by people in the building below to water plants or flush toilets.
sentences.chinese: 这些水可以被楼下的居民用来浇灌植物或冲厕所。

sentences.english: Sophisticated software can even tell the roofs to release water ahead of upcoming storms to maximise the system's ability to soak up rainwater.
sentences.chinese: 复杂巧妙的软件甚至可以在即将到来的风暴前指示屋顶释放水，以最大化系统吸收雨水的能力。

sentences.english: It can even identify which areas of the city are at most risk and tailor the response accordingly.
sentences.chinese: 它甚至可以识别城市中哪些区域风险最高，并相应调整应对措施。

sentences.english: Yu Kongjian describes the sponge city approach as using Tai Chi with nature instead of boxing.
sentences.chinese: 俞孔坚将海绵城市的方法描述为与自然打太极而不是拳击。

sentences.english: Questions have been raised as to whether a natural approach is sufficient when faced with increased rain fall globally.
sentences.chinese: 面对全球降雨量增加的情况，自然方法是否足够，人们提出了质疑。

sentences.english: What remains to be seen is whether increased scale and combination with modern technology can help natural methods save many more people from flooding.
sentences.chinese: 还有待观察的是，扩大规模并与现代技术相结合，能否帮助自然方法拯救更多人免受洪水之害。
